S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (dysthymia) is a chronic mood disorder characterized by a consistently low or dysthymic mood lasting at least two years in adults, with no extended periods of full remission. Individuals often function day-to-day but at a reduced level, experiencing a long-standing sense of gloom, low motivation, and other depressive features that become part of their perceived personality. Clinically, it differs from major depressive disorder by its chronicity and typically milder, more insidious presentation, though episodes of major depression can occur on top of it ("double depression"). It is frequently under-recognized because patients and families may attribute the symptoms to character or life circumstances rather than a treatable illness, and impairment is often seen in social, occupational, or academic domains over time.

patient.stressor: About three years ago, Lan took on a particularly demanding caseload when her agency lost two senior aides, leaving her covering more medically fragile, homebound elders with minimal backup. Around the same time, her mother in the South Bay began to decline with worsening diabetes and mobility issues, and Lan found herself driving down on weekends to coordinate appointments and manage her mother’s care, on top of her full-time job and community volunteering. Over the following 2-plus years, the combination of emotional labor at work, worry about her mother, and a gradual pulling back from her usual art, hiking, and cultural activities eroded her sense of balance and satisfaction, though she kept telling herself this was just what a devoted daughter and caregiver does. She finally agreed to see her primary care doctor after her husband and a younger aide she mentors both commented that she seemed to have lost her usual enthusiasm for patients and had started turning down museum outings and senior-center workshops that once energized her, prompting her provider to refer her for a psychiatric evaluation.
patient.chief_complaint: I feel like I’ve been stuck in this low, heavy mood for years and I just don’t enjoy anything the way I used to.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days it feels like there’s this gray film over everything, like even when I’m joking with my clients or sitting with my mom I’m watching myself go through the motions and underneath I just feel heavy and kind of hopeless, like this is just how life is going to be now.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: I used to be pretty steady with my weight, but over the past couple of years I’ll go all day at work barely touching my lunch because nothing sounds appealing, then come home and pick at crackers or cereal and call it dinner, and my clothes hang looser even though I’m not trying to lose weight.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I lie there for an hour or more with my mind running through my clients and my mom, finally fall asleep, then wake up at three or four in the morning and just stare at the ceiling feeling drained but unable to drift back off, so by the time my alarm goes off I feel like I’ve already put in a full day.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: I’m tired in a way that doesn’t match what I’ve done—just getting through a normal shift and then driving to check on my mom leaves me so wiped out that even simple things like folding laundry or setting up my paints on the weekend feel like climbing a hill, so I end up sitting on the couch instead.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: In the last couple of years I’ve started turning down extra shifts, art classes, and outings with friends because I just don’t have it in me, and even at work I catch myself doing the bare minimum and avoiding taking on new cases or projects I would have jumped at before.
add_requirements.duration: This low, heavy way of feeling has been hanging over me pretty steadily since I took on that bigger caseload and started caring for my mom more intensely a little over two years ago.
